title: 2015 Moncks Corner mid-air collision

route.from_name: Berkeley County Airport / Shaw Air Force Base

summary: An F-16 fighter jet descending for an instrument landing system approach collided in flight with a Cessna 150 climbing from Berkeley County Airport. Despite air traffic control warnings of opposite-direction traffic, the F-16 pilot was unable to locate the Cessna visually. The two aircraft collided at 1,450 feet over Moncks Corner, South Carolina. Both Cessna occupants were killed; the F-16 pilot ejected safely.
probable_cause: The approach controller's failure to provide an appropriate resolution to the conflict between the F-16 and the Cessna. (p. 2)

factors.evidence: The controller issued an ambiguous conditional instruction to turn left if traffic not in sight, then directed the F-16 pilot to turn left heading 180 immediately without ensuring the pilot had acquired visual contact. (p. 2)

The F-16 pilot responded that he was looking for the traffic but did not visually locate the Cessna before the collision; the pilot initiated a standard rate left turn using autopilot to continue visual search. (p. 2)

The Cessna was climbing under visual flight rules and was not in communication with FAA air traffic control, nor was the pilot required to be; the Cessna had not requested flight-following services. (p. 2)
The F-16 and Cessna 150 collided in-flight over Moncks Corner at approximately 1,450 feet altitude, about 40 seconds after the initial traffic advisory. (p. 2)

events.text: Charleston Approach controller issued traffic advisory to F-16 pilot: traffic 12 o'clock 2 miles opposite direction 1,200 feet, type unknown.
F-16 pilot responded looking for the traffic.
Controller issued conditional instruction to turn left heading 180 if traffic not in sight.
Controller issued direct instruction: if F-16 pilot did not have traffic in sight turn left heading 180 immediately.
F-16 pilot initiated standard rate left turn using autopilot to continue visual search for traffic.
Radar showed F-16 at 1/2 nautical mile northeast of Cessna at 1,500 feet while Cessna was at 1,400 feet on opposite track; airplanes continued to converge.
The two aircraft collided at approximately 1,450 feet altitude.
F-16 pilot ejected from aircraft and descended safely by parachute with minor injuries; Cessna destroyed with both occupants killed.
